details: The check of spec-review fixes reads artifacts only, so a finding whose failing case a few lines of code can run is marked MET after a fix that only narrowed it; the same defect came back as MEDIUM in the apply review and cost a second fix round.
failing_case: Trial spec review F1: scenarios did not cover brackets, underscore, backtick, so a 9-mark strip passes; the fix added 8 marks of 32; delegate:checker marked F1 MET by reading; sdd:reviewer then found that a mutant stripping 14 of the 32 ASCII marks passes all 15 tests.
pass_cases: The same F1 after a partial fix is reported open by the checker because its sketch still passes; a complete fix is MET.
reason: tests/test_roles.py::test_judge_check_runs_a_sketch_of_a_runnable_failing_case passes at head, fails at base 2a46798e (earlier check); unchanged by this fix.
findings.summary: A spec fix is marked met by reading, not by running

details: CONFIRMED by reading: checker.md "Write is only for your input file (a scratchpad or the worktree's `.ci/`)."
critic.md "Write is only for the TOML input file". Precedence part: "the project's rules for this agent win,
then the project's rules for your role, then the text of your flow in this file, then the shared text of your
role." The new rule sits in the shared text, the lowest rank. Whether a model actually skips the sketch is
PLAUSIBLE (no eval, see F2), but the text the item adds is the weakest of three conflicting texts.
Size: 10 agent minutes (two flow lines, one base line, relay sync, the text test).
evidence: -> "Write is only for your input file (a scratchpad or the worktree's `.ci/`). You never write a check mark"
critic.md flow: "Write is only for the TOML input file; `relay check record review --input <file>` writes ..."
grep -n 'Bash is for reading' roles/judge.md -> 25:- Bash is for reading, and for running one existing test or check that
failing_case: A checker gets a finding whose failing case is "strip_marks('[a]_`b`') keeps the brackets". The base (step 2)
now says: run it as a scratch script in the scratchpad. Its own flow part says "Write is only for your input
file (a scratchpad or the worktree's .ci/)", and the precedence part says the flow text wins over the shared
role text; the base Scope bullet also says "Bash is for reading, and for running one existing test or check".
Now: two instructions that forbid writing the script outrank the one that requires it; a checker that obeys
precedence reads and marks MET (the very failure of the item). Should: the flow part allows the sketch file.
fix_hint: checker.md: "Write is only for your input file and a check-step-2 sketch script, both in the scratchpad (or
the input in the worktree's .ci/)". Same in critic.md. In the judge base Scope bullet add "and, in check mode,
a sketch of a failing case (check step 2)". Extend the new test to assert the flow lines.
pass_cases: 1. checker.md flow part: the Write sentence names a scratch sketch script in the scratchpad beside the input file.
2. critic.md flow part ("Write is only for the TOML input file"): same allowance, since the critic carries check mode too.
3. roles/judge.md Scope bullet "Bash is for reading, and for running one existing test" names the check-mode sketch as allowed (or is scoped to review mode), in all five synced copies.
4. The checker still may not write in the worktree outside .ci/ (the sketch is outside the repo).
findings.summary: the checker's flow part still says Write is only for the TOML input, and its flow text outranks the base that now asks for a scratch script

details: CONFIRMED that no behavioural check exists: evals/scenarios has add-function, lookup, review-offbyone,
small-script; evals/plugin cases are front cases; evals/judge-measure grades review prose. Principle 5 (meaning
to the model is "tested with paid checks"), and the brief allowed one paid eval of one cheap case "if the fix
can only be shown that way", which is the case here: a text-presence test passes with the behaviour off.
Size: 30 agent minutes (one scenario on the review-offbyone model, one paid run under $1).
evidence: ls evals/scenarios -> add-function lookup review-offbyone small-script
git grep -n -i -l checker -- evals -> only evals/plugin/*/prompt.md front cases
worker report: "Check green (296 passed)" , no eval run named.
failing_case: Item pass case: "The same F1 after a partial fix is reported open by the checker because its sketch still
passes; a complete fix is MET." Disable the behaviour (a checker that ignores the new sentence and reads):
test_judge_check_runs_a_sketch_of_a_runnable_failing_case still passes, since it only greps the text.
No eval case under evals/ drives a checker at all (grep finds none), so the paid run after the wave does
not cover it either. Now: nothing shows the checker runs the sketch. Should: one cheap eval case shows it.
fix_hint: Add evals/scenarios/check-narrowed-fix (copy review-offbyone's scaffold): a tiny strip function, a review JSON
with the 32-mark failing case, a fix commit covering 8; grade that F1 is NOT MET with "sketch run:". Run it once.
pass_cases: 1. An eval case: a review JSON with F1 "strip removes all 32 ASCII marks", a fix that covers 8 marks; the checker's verdict for F1 is NOT MET and its reason holds "sketch run:".
2. Same case with a fix covering all 32: F1 MET, reason holds "sketch run:".
3. A finding whose failing case is prose only (a doc line): checked by reading, no sketch demanded.
4. The text test stays, as the cheap guard against the words being lost in a sync.
reason: Pass case 1 (narrowed fix reported NOT MET) is shown by one real run per the fixer (checker ran a scratch script, F1 NOT MET), but only in the fixer's report, not repeated by me. Cases 2 (complete fix is MET) and 3 (prose-only finding) have no scenario. The graders are weak: the scenario was not run with the behaviour off, a checker that only reads could also see "[" missing and pass f1-left-open, and the regex "sketch|scratch" matches any mention of the word, so it does not prove a script was run. The changed graders were not re-run with the model. Owner decides whether this one-run evidence is enough.
findings.summary: the item's pass case (a narrowed fix is reported open by the checker) is never shown: the only test checks that words exist

details: CONFIRMED by reading SKILL.md lines 71-83 and plugins/openspec/skills/plan/SKILL.md:66-75. Correct today in
intent; unclear on the one path the item names. Size: 5 agent minutes.
evidence: sed -n 60,100p plugins/openspec/skills/spec-review/SKILL.md -> "says so in its verdict" ... "The spec check writes no verdict"
failing_case: spec-review step 4, the path the item is about: "the checker runs that sketch ... and says so in its verdict",
and a few lines down "The spec check writes no verdict (it is not a merge)"; the checker flow: with
`Gate: none (artifacts only)` "the report writes no verdict ... a plain text file". The base says "say so in
the verdict reason". In openspec, plan/SKILL.md uses "sketch" for the picture saved in
openspec/changes/<change>/sketch/. Now: a checker of a spec review has no verdict reason to write into and
"that sketch" can be read as the saved design sketch. Should: "says so in the report's line for that finding
(sketch run: ...)", and a word not taken in openspec (a probe script).
fix_hint: "... the checker runs it as a scratch script outside the repo and writes `sketch run: <what it showed>` on
that finding's line of its report". Optionally say "probe" instead of "sketch" in both texts.
pass_cases: 1. SKILL.md step 4 names where the sketch result goes in the plain-text spec-check report.
2. The base's "verdict reason" wording also covers the plain-text report (or names it).
3. The word used for the script is not "sketch" in the openspec plugin, or is qualified ("a scratch script").
reason: Wording test in tests/test_roles.py, earlier check; unchanged.
findings.summary: spec-review says the checker reports the sketch 'in its verdict', but the spec check writes no verdict, and 'sketch' already names the saved design sketch in openspec
